No. Every matrix of the form $CC^T$ is symmetric, since $(CC^T)^T = (C^T)^T C^T = CC^T$. A linear combination of symmetric matrices is again symmetric, because $(\sum \lambda_i M_i)^T = \sum \lambda_i M_i^T = \sum \lambda_i M_i$. Therefore any linear combination of matrices of the form $CC^T$ must be symmetric.

However, a product $AB$ of two square matrices need not be symmetric. For a concrete counterexample, take over $\mathbb{R}$

$$A = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 \end{pmatrix}, \qquad B = \begin{pmatrix} 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 \end{pmatrix}.$$

Then

$$AB = \begin{pmatrix} 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 \end{pmatrix},$$

which is not symmetric ($(AB)^T \neq AB$). Hence this $AB$ cannot be expressed as a linear combination of matrices of the form $CC^T$.

Therefore, not every product $AB$ of two square matrices can be expressed as a linear combination of matrices of the form $CC^T$.

### PROOF COMPLETE
